headline: DoorDash says it has seen only several hundred orders from third-party AI agents
body: DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said on the company's third-quarter earnings call that it sees "maybe several hundred orders in total from some of these third-party agents." TechCrunch notes the company's 2025 report put its average at 3 million deliveries daily.
note: Early agentic commerce volume at a large consumer platform looks small next to its own app traffic, a useful yardstick for payment firms sizing agent-driven checkout.

evidence.text: Delivery company DoorDash revealed during its third-quarter earnings call that it has only seen “several hundred” orders from third-party agents like Muse, Instinct, Fo, and others.
For comparison, the company said in its 2025 report it completes an average of 3 million deliveries daily.
“What I mean by that is if you look at where AI agents are today, we’re seeing maybe several hundred orders in total from some of these third-party agents,” he said.
Xu mentioned that users are still predominantly placing orders through DoorDash’s app.
